name: lighthouse
description: Store files forever on IPFS/Filecoin via Lighthouse, paid per upload with x402 (USDC on Base, no account, no KYC): an unpaid upload answers HTTP 402 with `accepts`, the caller's wallet signs an EIP-3009 transfer, the retry with X-PAYMENT is verified before the bytes move and settled after the CID comes back. No API key to paste: the deployment mints its own from the box wallet, and the MCP server takes callers with no token. Every file shows up in your store with its sharing and permissions.
frontend: app/server.py (stdlib — the console at /lighthouse on :50681; proxies /lighthouse/_api to the API)

store.auth: the caller's own protocol token is forwarded — this module holds no store credential, so the store's whitelist, terms and quota apply to the address that actually signed
store.note: the store keeps the gateway url, so store /get redirects a reader straight at Lighthouse; no bytes are copied into the store

/price.docs: ?size=N → what an upload of N bytes costs THIS caller: {due, why, usd, units, x402: the exact 402 body /put would answer} — sign first, upload once

/pay.docs: GET the x402 policy (price, chains, USDC asset + EIP-712 domain, pay_to, facilitator, stats; owner also sees payments). POST (owner) change it off-chain

/status.docs: Module status: key configured, gateway, index size, auth mode, and the store link (whitelist / terms / quota when a token is sent)

/me.docs: Caller address, owner flag, which Lighthouse key this request would use, and the store's view of the caller

/key.docs: GET key status (+ remote validation, where the key came from: wallet / pasted / env); POST (owner) persist a dashboard key off-chain in ~/.mod/lighthouse/credentials.json. Neither is needed — with no key the box mints one from its own wallet on first use

/put.docs: Upload a file to Lighthouse (perpetual IPFS/Filecoin pin); form: key, register=true, public, pool. Paid with x402: no X-PAYMENT → 402 {x402Version, accepts[]}; sign one, retry with X-PAYMENT; receipt in X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE, `payment` in the body. Verified before upload, settled after, never charged for a failure. Free for the box, the owner token and x-lh-key. Registers the CID in the store only for a signed caller

/put/text.docs: Same as /put (and the same x402 gate) for a string body: {text, key, register, public, pool}

/get.docs: Stream a CID through the Lighthouse gateway (?download=1 to attach). Public by construction — access control is the store's job

/preview.docs: Peek at a CID: decoded text when it is text, size, truncated flag

/list.docs: This module's index: the caller's uploads — the `anon` rows without a token (?scope=all for every row, owner only)

/pin.docs: Record a CID in the index (Lighthouse uploads are already pinned perpetually)

/rm.docs: Drop a row from the index. Does NOT unpin — the pin is perpetual and the CID stays retrievable

/usage.docs: Remote data usage for the key this request is using

/uploads.docs: What Lighthouse itself lists under this key (?page=)

/store.docs: The store link from the caller's side: reachable, address, whitelisted, terms accepted, quota, and what still blocks a push

/store/terms.docs: The store's current terms text + version

/store/terms/accept.docs: Sign-accept the store terms — the caller's own token is forwarded as the proof, this module never signs for anybody

/store/register.docs: Reference an existing Lighthouse CID in the store: {cid, key, size, public, pool}. No bytes move

/store/objects.docs: The caller's store objects, Lighthouse-backed only unless ?all_backends=1

/store/mirror.docs: Make a store object perpetual: fetch it with the caller's token, upload to Lighthouse, register the CID back. Reports whether the CID came back identical

/mcp.docs: MCP. GET is the whole schema as a document (protocol, transports, auth, every tool inputSchema, client config); POST is the Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0 transport. Nothing is required to connect or call — no API key, no token. A tool that needs the store (register, objects, mirror, terms, forget) answers an isError result naming the Bearer token it wants; it is never a transport 401

/mcp/tools.docs: Just the tools: name, description, inputSchema, annotations, which auth and which transports each one accepts

/mcp/config.docs: Client config for this deployment — http block, stdio block, and the `claude mcp add` line, with the url as the caller reached it

byok.note: a per-request Lighthouse key, never written to disk and discarded when the request ends — how a visitor spends their own allowance instead of the deployment’s. Optional: the deployment has a key of its own, minted from the box wallet

transports.http: POST /mcp on the API — schema at GET /mcp
transports.stdio: python3 mcp.py — runs with this box’s own keys

mcp.auth: none required. A mod-protocol token as Authorization: Bearer is OPTIONAL — without it you are `anon`: lighthouse_status, lighthouse_preview, lighthouse_store, lighthouse_put, lighthouse_list, lighthouse_pin and lighthouse_account all work; lighthouse_terms, lighthouse_register, lighthouse_objects, lighthouse_mirror and lighthouse_forget need the token because they act in the store or on a signer's rows
mcp.byok: the `key` argument (or `api_key` on the upload tools) spends the caller’s Lighthouse account and is never written to disk
mcp.note: one implementation behind three faces — the MCP tools, the REST routes and the CLI all call mod.py and store_link.py, so the schema the console renders is the server’s own
mcp.keyless: the deployment's Lighthouse key is minted by the box from its own wallet (EIP-191 signature of Lighthouse's nonce → api key, kept 0600 off-chain), so neither the operator nor a caller has to hold one
mcp.x402: lighthouse_put / lighthouse_mirror without `payment` answer an isError result carrying the 402 body (accepts + price); sign one and call again with `payment` (or X-PAYMENT on the MCP request). Free over stdio, for the owner token, or with your own api_key

env.LIGHTHOUSE_API_KEY: API key from files.lighthouse.storage — optional, the box mints its own (or persist one via m lighthouse/set_key)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_AUTO_KEY: 1 (default) = mint a Lighthouse key from this box’s wallet when none is configured; 0 = never
env.LIGHTHOUSE_ANON_MAX_BYTES: largest upload an unsigned caller may make on the deployment key (default 8 MiB; 0 closes the anonymous door)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_ANON_DAILY_BYTES: rolling 24h budget for all unsigned uploads on the deployment key (default 256 MiB; 0 closes the anonymous door)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_DIR: State dir: credentials, owner claim, sqlite index (default ~/.mod/lighthouse)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_ACTIVATOR_URL: Fleet activator used to wake a slept store (default http://127.0.0.1:9000; empty string = never wake, just report it down)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_STORE_MODULE: Activator's name for the store module (default 'store')
env.LIGHTHOUSE_WAKE_TIMEOUT: Seconds to wait for a woken store's api port (default 45)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_OPEN: 1 = treat every caller as signed in (local development only)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_OWNER: Fallback owner address when ~/.mod/lighthouse/owner.json is absent
env.LIGHTHOUSE_PAY_TO: receiving EVM address for x402 upload payments (overrides ~/.mod/lighthouse/pay.json)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_FREE: 1 = turn x402 off: uploads are free again (anonymous ones within the anon budget)

credentials: ~/.mod/lighthouse/credentials.json (api_key + source: wallet|pasted, address) + owner.json (off-chain, never committed)

pay.protocol: x402 v1, scheme exact (EIP-3009 USDC transferWithAuthorization)
pay.note: public defaults; pay_to and overrides live off-chain in ~/.mod/lighthouse/pay.json (m lighthouse/pricing pay_to=0x…); ledger in ~/.mod/lighthouse/pay.db
